newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Eurodollars end weaker, supported near-term.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Eurodollars end weaker, supported near-term.

text.p: SIMEX Eurodollar futures finished weaker in thin trade on Wednesday but dealers said their downside was likely to be supported ahead of key U.S. data later in the week.
They said the market would scrutinise February retail sales and producer price data for indications of the Federal Reserve's likely stance at its March 25 policy making meeting.
"There's a decent chance they'll raise rates this time around because of what (Alan) Greenspan's been saying," a trader with a European bank said.
"A 25-basis point hike is pretty much priced in but quite a lot depends on the upcoming figures to determine whether they do it in March," he added.
September Eurodollars ended at 93.975 against their IMM close at 94.005 on volume of 4,705 lots.

Euroyen futures were stuck in a two-tick band despite strong gains in Japanese government bond (JGB) futures, with dealers attributing their sluggishness to a lack of market interest ahead of the Japanese financial year end on March 31.
"The Japanese are closing their books for the year end. And the foreigners are not buying either," the trader said.
September Euroyen was quoted at 99.32 at 1115 GMT against its IMM close at 99.31 on volume of 2,620 lots. December was at 99.20 against 99.19 on 1,800 lots.
June JGBs ended at 125.78 after setting a new high of 125.80 against their previous 125.62.
"When they failed to break below 125.61, some good buying interest emerged," a trader with a European futures house said.
He said the contract faced resistance at 125.80 and then at the psychological level of 126.00.
